facts.text: Dayton’s Thomas Marshall House, built in 1868, was the first National Register property in Armstrong County and now houses the local history museum.
Dayton became a borough in 1873, originating from Wayne Township, with its first cabin erected around 1823 and a post office opening in 1850.
The town was named for Revolutionary War hero Anthony Wayne, whose campaigns skirted the area that later became Dayton.
In 2025, Dayton added the Soldiers’ Orphans’ Home to the Civil War Trails, directing visitors to the Marshall House for veteran history.
Dayton’s annual fair, founded in 1880 by an early settler’s wife, still features livestock shows and crop judging, honoring its agricultural roots.
The 1905 Normal School building survived a 1970s renovation thanks to local advocacy, preserving Dayton’s educational heritage.
